newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian magistrate taken off minister's case.
newsitem.headline: Italian magistrate taken off minister's case.

text.p: An Italian public prosecutor has been taken off a trial of four men accused in an alleged plot against Public Works Minister and former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro, court officials said on Thursday.
They said prosecutor Fabio Salamone had been replaced by Raimondo Giustozzi after Di Pietro's lawyer requested his removal earlier this week on the grounds of incompatability.

The trial in the northern city of Brescia concerns an alleged plot to force Di Pietro to resign from the judiciary in December 1994 when he was a star member of Milan's elite pool of "Clean Hands" anti-graft investigators.

Among the defendants are two men close to conservative former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi -- his brother and business partner Paolo Berlusconi and Cesare Previti, who was defence minister in Berlusconi's government in 1994.
Both men deny charges of extortion.

The request for Salamone's removal followed a recommendation by the chief prosecutor in Brescia that Salamone may not be impartial because Di Pietro had previously led investigations into his brother Filippo.
Salamone also conducted inquiries last year into alleged malpractice by Di Pietro, who was cleared of any wrongdoing.
Di Pietro joined the centre-left government after April's general election but belongs to no political party.
He resigned from the judiciary in December 1994 shortly after the Clean Hands team accused Berlusconi of complicity in alleged corruption but has never explained why he quit.
Giustozzi asked for the trial to be adjourned while he studied the court documents. It is due to resume next month.
